non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (row State Store); More information
non_blocking.suggestion: The State Store row and the Consequences cite OQ-wasm-plugin-system-20 as though it exists. The owning document's Open questions stop at -19, and its State Store rule still says only "One blocking call per Plugin Policy per request before commit ... a second returns `ERR_BUDGET`", with no replay exception. The ADR does say "Proposed to the owning document", which is correct for a one-file task. The owning document still has to add OQ-wasm-plugin-system-20 and the replay sentence at conformance. Until it does, the ADR and its owning document disagree on the retry case, so track this in the conformance backlog.

With different keys, which parallel `aggregate` leg gets `ERR_BUDGET`, and therefore `RZ-PLG-006`, depends on which call arrives first. That is a race, and the Bad consequence mentions it only indirectly ("another key returns `ERR_BUDGET`"). Add a clause saying the losing leg is nondeterministic. Also consider an `ruralz bundle audit` finding for an Upstream-scoped `state.*` Plugin Policy attached to more than one Upstream, which is the case where keys usually differ per leg.

Pin the parameters of the streamed body read case. A 16 MiB body read through a 16 KiB buffer needs 1,024 `request_body_read` calls. That is more than the 1,000 Host Function calls per call (target) substitute budget, so it would get `ERR_BUDGET` and then `RZ-PLG-006`. Copying more than 16 MiB also uses a large share of the 5 ms `limits.timeout` (target). State the chunk size (for example 64 KiB), `limits.memoryBytes` and `limits.timeout` for the case, so the test proves streaming and does not trip the budget or the deadline.

`chunk_read` takes `(o, c, out i32)` and has no offset, yet the row groups it with the offset reads. Say how a chunk larger than `c` is continued: an implicit cursor per call, or truncation. Otherwise PDKs will implement different behavior before the freeze.

Plugins can only write State Store values through `state_incr`, as i64 values under their own `rzplg:` prefix. So `state_get` output is bounded, and a guest never needs the full-length retry, which would count as a second blocking call. State the encoding (for example, decimal ASCII of at most 20 bytes) so that PDKs size the buffer once and never issue a second `state_get` that triggers `ERR_BUDGET`.

Tag the derived figures as the owning document does: "the 2 GiB default cap (target)" and "a 4 GiB cap (target)". The 12 comes from N = 16 minus ceil(16/4) = 4 under a 50% share (target), so it inherits that tag.

At 1,000 contexts per instance (target) and a 1 ms (target) pinned wait, one guest call that runs to the 5 ms `limits.timeout` (target) fails every queued pinned call with `RZ-PLG-005`. Consider saying that the adapter assigns new contexts to the least-loaded instance and caps contexts per instance by measured call rate, not only by the fixed 1,000. Record this under OQ-wasm-plugin-system-17.

ac_results.ac: Front matter contains id, title, status, date, deciders and related, and status matches this manifest.
ac_results.note: The front matter has id ADR-0005, a title identical to the manifest title, status accepted (matches the manifest), date 2026-09-25, deciders [ruralz-core], and a related list that includes the owning document and the depends_on files.

ac_results.ac: H2 headings match adr_common.outline_h2 exactly and in order, and Decision outcome contains the H3 headings Consequences and Confirmation.
ac_results.note: The six H2 headings appear in the manifest order, and Consequences and Confirmation are H3 headings under Decision outcome. verify-docs prints no FAIL line for this file. Its only output is four WARN milestones lines about roadmap items, and the length is within the 400 to 1,500 band.

ac_results.ac: Considered options lists at least two options including the chosen one, and each has pros and cons.
ac_results.note: Three options are listed: the custom capability-based ABI, proxy-wasm as the primary ABI, and the Extism go-sdk as host. Each has Good and Bad bullets, and all 11 distinct URLs appear in the research files.

ac_results.ac: Decision outcome states the chosen option as 'Chosen option: ..., because ...' and matches the foundation pack section 7 row for this ADR.
ac_results.note: The chosen option quotes the manifest decision verbatim and matches the pack section 7 Plugin ABI row: custom capability-based Plugin ABI v1, Extism-style memory and Host Function conventions, and a proxy-wasm compatibility adapter Planned (M4).

ac_results.ac: Confirmation names a concrete verification mechanism (test, lint rule, CI gate or review checklist item).
ac_results.note: Confirmation names the Plugin ABI conformance suite in `pr-full`, which now covers the streamed body read, the retry and `aggregate` State Store replay, and sticky errors. It also names the adapter conformance suite, Planned (M4), with the fault-radius and pinned-wait cases, the online Plugin check (RZ-CFG-028), Host Function fuzzing, the SM-6 gate and a review checklist item.

ac_results.ac: The ADR is linked from docs/adr/README.md and from its owning document.
ac_results.note: The owning document links the ADR in Contract and in proxy-wasm stance. docs/adr/README.md does not exist yet because the index is written later with docs/README.md, so this is not a defect in the ADR text and does not block.
